system_overview: This specification models a parameterized, partially synchronous system implementing an eventually perfect failure detector, based on Chandra and Toueg (1996). It serves as an environment controller that composes two sub-specifications: an age-tracking communication channel and the per-process failure detector logic. The controller manages a global environmental clock, process crashes, message delivery, and enforces the partial synchrony constraints on message delay and relative process speeds.
actors_and_components: The system has three layers: (1) An environment controller managing a global clock, crash tracking, and partial synchrony constraints. (2) A communication channel that wraps messages in age-tracked boxes and supports pickup, delivery, and aging operations. (3) A set of N processes (numbered 1 through N), each running a failure detector that sends alive messages, receives messages, and makes failure predictions. Up to T processes may crash. The environment controller orchestrates interactions between these layers.
state_variables: The system tracks state across three layers. Communication layer: the set of age-tracked message boxes in transit, and the set of messages being delivered in the current transition. Process layer: for each process, a suspicion set, adaptive timeout intervals for each other process, last-heard counters, a local clock, and outgoing messages. Environment layer: for each process, a pause counter tracking how long since its last transition; a movement indicator recording what action the process last took (none, initialized, send, receive, predict, or crash); a crash flag indicating whether the process has crashed; and a global count of total failures so far.
initial_state: No messages are in transit or being delivered. No process suspects any other. All timeout intervals are set to a default value. All last-heard counters are zero. All local clocks are zero. No outgoing messages exist. All process pause counters are zero. All movement indicators show initialized. No process has crashed. The failure count is zero.
actions: Three top-level actions: (1) Crash: A non-crashed process crashes if the total failure count is below the maximum allowed. The process is marked as crashed, the failure count increases, its movement is recorded as crash, and its pause counter is set to a sentinel value. No channel or process-layer state changes. (2) Environmental tick: If at least one correct process took a transition in the previous tick, the global clock advances. All in-transit message ages increase by one. All movement indicators reset to none. All non-crashed process pause counters increase by one. (3) Process tick: A non-crashed process that has not yet moved in the current tick takes one action. Its pause counter resets to zero. It either (a) predicts which processes have crashed based on its timeout intervals, (b) sends alive messages to all processes and the channel picks up the messages destined for non-crashed processes, or (c) receives messages delivered by the channel and updates its suspicion list and timeout intervals accordingly. Crashed processes may also have messages delivered from the channel (to prevent unbounded message aging), but these messages are not processed. All three top-level actions are constrained by partial synchrony: the relative speed constraint requires that no correct process pauses for more than a bound on relative speed, and the message delay constraint requires that no message destined for a receiving process has an age exceeding the delay bound when that process performs a receive.
safety_properties: Type invariant: All process-layer and channel-layer variables conform to their types. Pause counters for correct processes are bounded. Crash flags and pause counters are consistent (crashed processes have sentinel pause values). The failure count is between zero and the maximum. Timeout intervals and message ages are bounded by computed upper limits derived from the timing parameters. Last-heard counters are bounded.
liveness_properties: Strong Completeness: Eventually, every crashed process is permanently suspected by every correct process. Eventually Strong Accuracy: There is a point in time after which no correct process is suspected by any other correct process. Together these define an eventually perfect failure detector.
model_bounds: N = 3 processes, T = 1 maximum failures, default timeout d0 = 2, send interval = 2, predict interval = 3, message delay bound = 1, relative speed bound = 1. With these parameters, TLC verification takes approximately 2 hours.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on the combined environmental tick and process tick actions, subject to both the message delay and relative speed constraints. The send and predict intervals must be positive and must not be multiples of each other. The specification uses a finite encoding of local clocks (resetting when exceeding all thresholds) and bounded counters to make the state space finite for model checking. Upper bounds on message ages and timeout intervals are computed from the timing parameters.
